title: Superconductivity and Magnetism in Bi-Ni System: From Bulk to Heterostructures
authors: Gabriel Sant'Ana, Yutao Xing, Milton A. Tumelero
abstract: Unconventional superconductivity with ingredients of magnetism such as time reversal breaking, triplet pairing and proximity effects has been a long time pursued topic in physics and material science as a new source of innovative phenomena and effects to drive further scientific advances and technologies. The Bi-Ni system has emerged as a convenient candidate for the investigation of such phenomenology. Strictly speaking, the term Bi-Ni system refers to two different schemes, first to the NiBi$_{3}$ intermetallic compound, a 4 K superconductor in which a complex magnetism seems to govern electrical properties in the normal phase, but without implication in the superconducting properties. The second Bi-Ni system is not quite a material but a heterostructure formed by a bilayer of Bi and Ni. Here the superconducting phase has to steal the spotlight by showing strong evidence of time-reversal breaking and triplet pairing featuring a complex unconventional state. The ease of preparing the samples, compared to other candidates for such unconventionality, usually Uranium-based compounds, has accelerated the research in this system. Here, we went through a detailed review of the main results about the electronic properties of these two systems as well as a discussion of the main open questions to be solved in order to reach the complete understanding in this topic.
summary: This review synthesizes decades of research on superconductivity and magnetism in $	ext{Bi-Ni}$ compounds and bilayers. It contrasts findings suggesting conventional $s$-wave superconductivity with strong evidence for unconventional, time-reversal symmetry breaking states. The work highlights the critical role of dimensionality and interfacial effects in modifying these fundamental electronic properties.
main_problem: The paper investigates the complex interplay between unconventional superconductivity and magnetism in the Bi-Ni system, specifically addressing the nature of magnetic anomalies in $	ext{NiBi}_3$ and the superconducting state in $	ext{Bi/Ni}$ bilayers.
main_result: The research presents conflicting evidence: some measurements suggest intrinsic time-reversal symmetry breaking and triplet pairing in the bilayer, while other studies point towards conventional $s$-wave superconductivity in the bulk $	ext{NiBi}_3$, highlighting a major unresolved conflict in the field.
method: The study synthesizes results from multiple techniques, including magnetotransport measurements (MR, anomalous Hall effect), magnetometry ($	ext{MOKE}$, $\mu	ext{SR}$), and spectroscopic probes (Andreev spectroscopy).
model_or_system: The focus is on two physical systems: the $	ext{NiBi}_3$ intermetallic compound (bulk and nanostructured) and the $	ext{Bi/Ni}$ heterostructure bilayer. The physics involves strong spin-orbit coupling ($	ext{SOC}$) and dimensionality effects.
key_observables: Superconducting critical temperature ($T_c$), magnetic hysteresis loops, nonreciprocal transport signals, and the deviation of the upper critical field ($	ext{H}_{c2}$) from the Pauli limit.
important_parameters: Low temperatures ($\sim 4 	ext{ K}$), high magnetic fields ($	ext{up to } 60 	ext{ T}$), and the ratio of in-plane vs. out-of-plane magnetic field responses.
main_assumptions: The analysis often compares experimental results against theoretical models, such as BCS theory for superconductivity and various limits ($	ext{B}_{	ext{P}}$, $	ext{B}^*_{	ext{P}}$) for magnetic field effects.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the orthorhombic structure of $	ext{NiBi}_3$, comparing magnetic measurements (ESR, moment vs. field) in bulk versus nanostructured samples, and showing the superconducting response to magnetic fields in both $	ext{NiBi}_3$ and $	ext{Bi/Ni}$ bilayers.
paper_structure: The review systematically examines the electronic properties of the two $	ext{Bi-Ni}$ systems, detailing experimental findings on magnetism (bulk vs. confined) and superconductivity (conventional vs. unconventional/topological), culminating in a discussion of open questions.
why_interesting: The interplay between superconductivity and magnetism, especially when mediated by strong spin-orbit coupling and dimensionality effects, is a core topic in strongly correlated electron physics, relevant to understanding exotic pairing symmetries.
